payload.label: L5-F1
payload.location: Report §Technical Foundations > JSON Numeric Loss; §Analysis > H1
payload.text: Blue claims JSON number precision loss above 2^53 is a failure mode. However, event logs store timestamps as ISO 8601 strings ('ts':'2026-07-20T08:08:21.265133000Z'), not JSON numbers. JSON.stringify does not lose precision on strings. Verified: all events-*.jsonl files use string serialization for ts. Failure mode should be removed from H1 risk assessment.

payload.label: L5-F2
payload.text: Blue cites 'Event drop already observed: bench closures were dropped' with footnote pointing to frontier.md §H4. However, frontier.md §H4 is a HYPOTHESIS section ('If H4 is FALSE...'), not observed fact. Spot-check: all 20 events across events-*.jsonl files have ts fields present. No events missing. Claim is speculative, not verified.

payload.label: L5-F3
payload.text: H1 (Deterministic Rendering) graded CERTAIN failure; H2 (Causal Consistency) also graded CERTAIN. These are in logical tension: if determinism fails (different renders), then causality is also deterministic (even if wrong). If causality is undefined, determinism should also fail. Are these independent? Root-cause relationship? Report does not clarify. Grading opacity obscures actual risk structure.

payload.label: L5-F4
payload.text: Blue dismisses event-sourcing libraries on 'licensing concerns' without verification. Most battle-tested libraries (EventStoreDB, Axon) use permissive licenses (MIT/Apache). No cost-benefit comparing build-vs-integrate time provided. Alternative dismissed too quickly.

payload.label: L5-F5
payload.text: Blue claims 'Each patch addressed one failure mode but introduced new ones' but provides zero examples. Did Blue actually try these fixes or only speculate? No code diffs, simulation results, or documented attempts provided. Claim of futility is unsubstantiated. Reader cannot verify whether attempts were genuine failures or prematurely abandoned.

payload.label: L5-F6
payload.text: Blue claims schema evolution breaks old events but does not verify whether frank-exchange-of-views schema has actually changed. Cites principle (correct) but not verified in feov-record. Event model is round-0 only; no historical schema changes documented. Failure mode is plausible but unverified in THIS tool.

payload.label: L5-F7
payload.location: Report §Technical Foundations > Clock and Timestamp Hazards
payload.text: Blue correctly states NTP can adjust clocks but does not verify: (a) whether NTP is enabled in deployment, (b) whether step vs. slew adjustments are used (modern systems use slew), or (c) actual risk window under deployment constraints. Claim is theoretically possible, not verified as likely under actual operating conditions.

payload.label: L5-F8
payload.text: feov-record is a Go binary (closed-source). Blue claims it 'does not document fsync enforcement' but provides no evidence of reading source code or documentation. Assumption about closed-source binary internals. Verification requires source-code inspection or tool-level testing, neither provided.

payload.label: L5-F9
payload.text: Logical tension: Report grades proposed event model CERTAIN failure then argues against building it because it's too complex. Clearer argument: 'Model would be unsound (CERTAIN failures) AND current model is adequate, therefore building unsound model is wasteful.' That's the real claim but not stated clearly. Model critique is valid but separate from decision not to build.
